haiku-low.q1: Held 10 minutes (configuration). A timer each minute marks an unclaimed hold EXPIRED and puts the stock back on sale. A later claim retakes stock, refused if any line is short.
haiku-low.q2: Before charging. Inventory reserves all lines first. If any line is short, nothing is reserved, the order is REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is told which items are short, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as provider idempotency key. Payment resends with the same key, so the provider returns the original charge. Payment also has a unique order_id constraint.
haiku-low.q4: The order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK with refund_status REFUND_PENDING. The customer gets a full refund and an email saying it was cancelled as out of stock.
haiku-low.q5: Only on OrderConfirmed, and Cart removes just the ordered lines and quantities. If checkout fails, the cart is untouched and the customer can retry with one press.
haiku-low.q6: Order coordinates each step and records state. Its orders table, status history and outbox hold how far each checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment, which verifies the signature, records the outcome and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event that Order consumes.
haiku-low.q8: Payment inserts the event id into processed_webhooks in the same transaction as the update, so repeats are ignored and get a 200. Consumers are idempotent, so repeated messages change nothing.
haiku-low.q9: Order marks CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled. Inventory then releases the reservation: HELD becomes RELEASED with stock back on sale, EXPIRED becomes RELEASED with no stock change.
haiku-low.q10: Order acts on its current status. AWAITING_PAYMENT starts a claim, which retakes stock if expired and confirms only if all lines are in stock. Otherwise it refunds in full. CONFIRMED is ignored.
haiku-low.q11: Payment retries the refund with key refund:+order id, with growing delays, and never stops. Ops is alerted at the attempt limit. Tracked in Payment's refunds table; Order shows REFUND_PENDING. Limits are NOT STATED.
haiku-low.q12: The OrderConfirmed event, carrying the snapshot's lines, causes Cart to remove those lines or reduce their quantities. Cart is the service that does it.

sonnet.q1: Held 10 minutes (expiry timer runs each minute, so up to a minute longer). If still HELD it becomes EXPIRED and stock goes back on sale; a later claim retakes the lines if all in stock, otherwise it is refused and the reservation is RELEASED.
sonnet.q2: Reserved before the charge (reserve, then AWAITING_PAYMENT, then Payment charges). If any line is short, nothing is reserved, the order is marked REJECTED_OUT_OF_STOCK, the customer is told which items are short, and payment is never requested.
sonnet.q3: The charge uses the order id as an idempotency key sent to the provider, so the provider returns the original charge; payments.order_id is also unique.
sonnet.q4: The claim is refused (reservation set RELEASED); the order becomes CANCELLED_OUT_OF_STOCK, refund_status REFUND_PENDING, a full refund is requested, and the customer is emailed that it was cancelled and a full refund is on its way.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only on OrderConfirmed, and only of the snapshotted lines (later additions stay). When checkout fails (rejected, cancelled, declined) the cart is untouched.
sonnet.q6: Order is the coordinator and starts each step. The record is Order's own database: order status (with status history, snapshot lines, outbox, and fields such as payment_succeeded_at, claim_started_at, refund_status).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment's endpoint (signature verified); Payment records the outcome and writes an outbox row, a relay publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined as an event on the broker, and Order handles it.
sonnet.q8: Payment inserts the webhook event id into processed_webhooks (unique) in the same transaction as the payment update; a repeat is ignored with a 200. Consumers are idempotent, and Order acts on the current status (CONFIRMED ignores a repeat PaymentSucceeded).
sonnet.q9: The reservation is released and stock goes back on sale. Order marks CANCELLED_PAYMENT_DECLINED and publishes OrderCancelled, which Inventory handles (HELD becomes RELEASED with stock back; EXPIRED becomes RELEASED with no stock change).
sonnet.q10: Order sends a claim to Inventory. With the reservation EXPIRED, Inventory tries to retake every line in one transaction: if all in stock it takes them and sets CLAIMED (order confirmed); if any line is short it takes nothing, sets RELEASED and refuses (order cancelled out of stock and fully refunded).
sonnet.q11: Payment marks it FAILED_RETRYING, increments attempts and sets next_attempt_at with growing delay; the retry worker keeps retrying. At the attempt limit it alerts ops once and keeps retrying at a slow fixed interval, never stopping; ops can force Retry now. Tracked in Payment's refunds table (and Order's refund_status records REFUND_PENDING until REFUNDED). Limit, backoff and interval values are NOT STATED.
sonnet.q12: The OrderConfirmed event (carrying the snapshot's cart line ids and quantities) causes it; the Cart service removes the lines or reduces quantities, recording the order id in processed_events for idempotency.
